short: The primary collection of examples a machine learning model inspects during training to adjust its internal parameters.
eli5: All the practice problems and study books you use to learn a subject before taking any exam.
example: Curating 100,000 deduplicated code snippets and docstrings for code-model training.

short: A held-out subset of data used during development to tune hyperparameters, select architectures, and catch overfitting early.
eli5: Mock quizzes you take halfway through studying to see which topics still need work before the real final.
example: Stopping training when validation loss starts rising even though training loss keeps falling.

short: A strictly locked-away dataset evaluated only once at the end to measure unbiased real-world model performance.
eli5: The sealed final exam you never peek at while studying, proving what you truly learned.
example: Reporting final F1-score on 5,000 freshly collected, unseen customer support transcripts.

short: Detecting and fixing corrupted records, duplicates, missing values, and formatting inconsistencies before modeling.
eli5: Checking a bowl of berries and tossing out bruised or moldy ones before baking a pie.
example: Removing boilerplate cookie banners and near-duplicate web pages from an LLM pretraining corpus.

short: Transforming raw data fields into informative numerical signals that make patterns easier for models to learn.
eli5: Turning raw birthdates into 'age' and 'is_weekend' clues so a model spots habits immediately.
example: Computing rolling 7-day average spend and ratio-to-limit features for fraud detection.

short: The fraction of total predictions a model gets right—clear for balanced classes, but misleading when one class is rare.
eli5: Your simple percentage score on a quiz—though if 99% of emails aren't spam, always guessing 'not spam' scores 99% while catching zero spam!
example: Measuring accuracy on balanced 10-class digit recognition where every digit appears equally often.

short: Precision measures how many positive flags were truly positive; recall measures how many real positives the model successfully caught.
eli5: Precision asks 'when the smoke alarm rings, is there really a fire?'; recall asks 'out of all real fires, how many did the alarm catch?'
example: Medical screening prioritizing high recall so dangerous conditions are rarely missed.

short: The harmonic mean of precision and recall, rewarding models that balance both catching positives and avoiding false alarms.
eli5: A combined report-card grade that drops sharply if either your precision OR your recall is sloppy.
example: Scoring Named Entity Recognition extractors where exact entity spans matter on imbalanced text.

short: A table comparing predicted labels against actual labels so you can see exactly which classes get mistaken for one another.
eli5: A grid showing not just your total score, but whether you keep confusing 'leopards' with 'cheetahs'.
example: Discovering a support router sends 'billing dispute' tickets into 'refund request' 18% of the time.

short: Exponentiated cross-entropy loss measuring how surprised a language model is by real text—lower perplexity means better prediction.
eli5: The average number of words the model feels torn between at each blank; perplexity of 5 means it's roughly guessing among 5 choices.
example: Comparing two pretrained checkpoints on held-out Wikipedia articles to track language modeling progress.

short: A standardized suite of tasks, datasets, and scoring metrics used to compare different models consistently.
eli5: An Olympic obstacle course that every runner runs under the exact same rules so times can be fairly compared.
example: Evaluating coding models on SWE-bench or reasoning models on standardized math competitions.

short: When information from the test set or future outcomes accidentally leaks into training, inflating scores without real skill.
eli5: Accidentally slipping tomorrow's exam answer key into tonight's study packet—you'll score 100% now and fail in real life.
example: Benchmark test questions appearing verbatim inside web-scraped LLM pretraining corpora.
